lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Hi, Daniel. Could you do me a favor?

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: I was walking to Riverside Park when one of my paper bags tore. Nothing broke, but I'm holding fruit, cups and two containers. I could really use your help.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: At the bus stop on Pine Street, near the pharmacy. Could you bring an empty tote bag?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: No problem. I can do that. I'm leaving now.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Thanks. Aisha might get to the park before us. Would you mind texting her? Tell her we're running about ten minutes late.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: I'll text her now. We could ask her to save a table.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Good idea. I really appreciate it.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Happy to help. I should be there in five minutes. Let me know if you need anything else.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: The bag is all I need. See you soon.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: I'm glad you made it. I was setting out the food when Daniel's message arrived.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Thanks for waiting. And Daniel, thanks for helping me out. I owe you one.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Don't worry about it. Carrying a tote bag for one block isn't a major rescue.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: It looked important from the message.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: It was important. Next time, I'm going to pack everything in one tote bag.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Good plan. I'm glad the apples made it.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: And our table. The new plan worked.
